The customer solution clearly answers with the book count.","judgment":"uncertain"},{"pair_id":"J03226","case1_error":"Uses one bottle's 80-load capacity as the total capacity of two bottles, instead of 160 loads.","case2_error":"Treats 32 ounces as pounds, multiplies by 16, and reverses the roles of total fruit and non-peach fruit.","reason":"One fails to scale capacity by bottle count; the other misassigns units and quantities in the subtraction.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03227","case1_error":"Treats 70% cheaper as paying 70% of the original price, rather than 30%.","case2_error":"Omits the additional 20% bulk discount when calculating savings.","reason":"Misinterpreting a discount percentage differs from entirely omitting an additional discount.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03228","case1_error":"Treats 70% cheaper as paying 70% of the original price, rather than 30%.","case2_error":"Subtracts redeemed coupons from the amount paid instead of adding them back; also labels a dollar amount as cents.","reason":"The first confuses the discount with the remaining price. The second reverses reconstruction of the original price and mishandles units.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03229","case1_error":"Uses an incorrect conversion factor of 1.16 ounces per pound instead of 16.","case2_error":"Subtracts dog eyes from an already-net eaten count, then divides 22 eyes among people without converting eyes to fish.","reason":"An explicitly incorrect conversion factor differs from omitting conversion and confusing the net count with the total.","judgment":"different"}]}
